title: Outside contracts on the school board's agendas
question: What do the school board's published agendas show about outside contracts, and how often was a contract brought for approval after the work had begun?
finding: 6,649 agenda items since January 2018 concern contracts, but only 266 carry a dollar figure that could be read, and most of those are the approval threshold or a bond ceiling, not a contract price: the contract lists sit on item pages that could not be downloaded, so the largest contracts by vendor cannot be ranked from these records. 336 items call a contract "retroactive" (work begun before approval): 168 in 2021-22, 5 in 2025-26 and 27 in the first four months of 2026-27. Who brought them: individual schools 119; other central offices 98; buildings and construction 48; special education services 45; unit not stated in the title 26. That is 252 more than the 84 counted on the other-public-bodies screen, which read a shorter extract. 22 organizations that carry findings or warning signs in the City data also appear on school or City College agendas; they are listed on the other-public-bodies screens.
how: Every agenda item of the Board of Education from January 2018 to 10 November 2026 whose title concerns a contract, agreement, purchase, change order, lease or warrants, counted by fiscal year; items whose title contains the word "retroactive"; and the unit named in the title as submitting it. The individual retroactive items, the largest authorisations at each body and the flagged organizations are on the screens "after-the-fact", "largest-elsewhere" and "flagged-elsewhere" of the add-backs and other-bodies file (the site’s “Earmarks, bids and other public bodies” page) and are not repeated here.
limits: Bringing a contract to the board after work has started is provided for in the district's own rules (one title cites Administrative Regulation 3312) and can follow from an urgent placement for a pupil with disabilities, a late grant or a slow approval calendar. The word first appears in agenda titles on 2021-04-06; its absence before then is a change of labelling, not evidence that no contract was late. Many of the contracts are small ones made by a single school, some with individual tutors or artists, who are not named here. A title is a proposal: an item can be withdrawn or amended. Contract amounts, vendors of batch items and the monthly lists of contracts under and over the approval threshold are on item pages and attachments that were not obtained, so this screen counts items and cannot rank money.
